text.title: Tailwind Patterns with CVA Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether Tailwind actually owns styling, on whether the codebase clears the reuse threshold a variant schema needs, and on whether custom scales exist that tailwind-merge cannot resolve — to the full cva pattern, a merge-config-first pass, or skip.

decision-tree.root-question: Is Tailwind in the build pipeline and the primary styling mechanism, rather than CSS-in-JS or vanilla-extract?

conclusion.verdict: skip; use the styling library's own recipe/variant API, which already gives typed variants and scoped class names

branch.question: Are there roughly 5 or more reusable components, each with more than one style axis (intent, size, state)?

conclusion.verdict: skip; below the reuse threshold there are no conflicts to resolve — a single-use component's ternary is cheaper than a variant schema

branch.question: Does the design system add custom utilities or scale keys (`text-display-lg`, `shadow-card`, plugin-generated classes) that `tailwind-merge` does not know by default?

conclusion.verdict: apply, but register the custom class groups via `extendTailwindMerge` first — otherwise a consumer override silently loses to the component's own class
apply in full: one module-scope `cva` call per component, literal class names only, `cn(variants(...), className)` order, compound variants for cross-axis cases, defaults on every axis
